messages:
oliver: Heads-up — after rolling the base image to ubuntu:24.04 + nvidia-container-toolkit 1.12, a bunch of training pods are crashing on start. containers report missing vendor libs, e.g. "error loading libnvidia-ml.so.1: No such file or directory". :eyes:

maya: Which cluster/region? any node driver upgrades recently?

oliver: us-west-2 batch pool. No driver change on host level from our side — drivers are 535.xx installed on nodes last month. The only change was the base image + toolkit package in our infra-buildkite job.

ralph: Can you paste the container runtime error (dmesg / containerd logs)? sounds like bind mount propagation or runtime hook failing to inject libs.

oliver: Paste of the short log snippet:
```
rpc error: code = Unknown desc = failed to start containerd task: OCI runtime create failed: container_linux.go:...: starting container process caused: process_linux.go:...: stat /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libnvidia-ml.so.1: no such file or directory
```
Also from kubelet: `failed to setup device plugin: nvidia-container-toolkit: hook failed: exit status 1`

anya: Reproduced on a small GKE-like test node in eu-central-1. If you exec into the node the host has `/usr/lib/nvidia-535/libnvidia-ml.so.1` but container path expected is different. Looks like the toolkit runtime is not mapping host vendor lib dir into the container root.

maya: Two quick things to check: 1) mountPropagation on the daemonset volumes, 2) `nvidia-container-runtime` config for lib paths. We recently switched to the toolkit's new auto-detect mode in the image.

ralph: Also check `/etc/nvidia-container-runtime/config.toml` on the node — the `disable-requirements`/`ldconfig` flags changed across toolkit versions. If the runtime refuses to bind an alternate library path it will error like that.

oliver: I tried toggling mountPropagation to `Bidirectional` on the device plugin DS — no dice. The device plugin logs show the hook ran but then containerd returns `ENOENT` for the path inside container.

maya: Can you share the pod spec? sometimes we accidentally set `readOnlyRootFilesystem: true` which blocks the runtime from writing the symlinks.

oliver: Pod snippet (sanitized):
```
volumeMounts:
 - name: nvidia-driver
   mountPath: /var/lib/nvidia
   mountPropagation: Bidirectional
   readOnly: true
securityContext:
  readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
```

anya: Aha — readOnlyRootFilesystem + readonly vendor mount makes the runtime unable to create symlink at `/usr/lib/...` inside container. The previous toolkit had fallback logic to use `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`, new one prefers in-container symlinks.

ralph: Quick workaround: remove `readOnlyRootFilesystem` (or make readOnly false for that mount) or mount the driver libs into a different path that is already present and writable. We should also try pinning the toolkit package back to 1.10 on the infra-image.

oliver: Can confirm removing `readOnlyRootFilesystem` for the pod fixed startup in staging. Prod patch rolling now.

deploy-bot: deploy pipeline #infra/base-image 2026-03-18T15:02:10Z — rolled back infra-image tag `infra-v2026-03-18-toolkit1.12` -> `infra-v2026-03-10-toolkit1.10` by oliver :white_check_mark:

maya: For a durable fix we should: 1) update our daemonset generator to set the driver mount writable, 2) add a preflight check that validates toolkit/runtime can write symlinks into container root, 3) add a canary job that runs minimal CUDA smoke tests after base image updates.

ralph: Filed infra ticket: INFRA-1723 — "toolkit 1.12: runtime fails to map driver libs into readonly containers". Assigning to eng-infra.

sre-bot: Noted: kernel-driver mismatch alert on us-west-2 nodes (driver 535 vs kernel 6.3) — monitoring spike for `cudaGetDeviceCount` errors. Recommend scheduling a driver stability window.

anya: Also seeing some NCCL init logs in the crashed pods: `NCCL WARN: Init call failed: invalid device pointer` — probably a downstream symptom of missing nvml.

oliver: Rolling changeback + ticketed follow-ups. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
